front: Preamble of the Constitution: Key Dates & Source
back:
• Drafted based on: 'Objective Resolution' moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on 13 Dec 1946 (adopted 22 Jan 1947).
• Adopted on: 26 November 1949 (celebrated as Constitution Day / Samvidhan Divas).
• Came into full force: 26 January 1950 (Republic Day).
• Borrowed idea from: USA (Language inspired by Australia).
• Status: Declared an integral part of the Constitution in Kesavananda Bharati case (1973).

front: Preamble: 42nd Amendment 1976 Changes & Keywords Sequence
back:
• Sequence of words in Preamble: 'SOVEREIGN, SOCIALIST, SECULAR, DEMOCRATIC, REPUBLIC'.
• 3 Words added by 42nd Amendment Act 1976:
  1. Socialist (समाजवादी)
  2. Secular (धर्मनिरपेक्ष/पंथनिरपेक्ष)
  3. Integrity (अखंडता)
• Preamble has been amended ONLY ONCE in history (42nd Amendment 1976).

front: Doctrine of 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution
back:
• Landmark Case: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (24 April 1973, 13-Judge Bench - largest ever).
• Ruling: Parliament has power to amend Constitution under Art 368, but CANNOT alter or destroy its 'Basic Structure'.
• Basic features include: Supremacy of Constitution, Rule of Law, Judicial Review, Secularism, Federalism, Free & Fair elections.

front: Sources of Indian Constitution: UK & USA
back:
• From United Kingdom (UK / Britain):
  - Parliamentary system of government
  - Rule of Law (Article 14)
  - Single Citizenship (एकल नागरिकता)
  - Cabinet system & Prerogative Writs
  - Bicameralism (दो सदनों वाली संसद)

• From United States of America (USA):
  - Fundamental Rights (Part III)
  - Independent Judiciary & Judicial Review
  - Impeachment of President (Art 61)
  - Removal of SC and HC judges
  - Post of Vice-President & Preamble

front: Sources of Indian Constitution: Ireland, Australia, Germany, USSR, South Africa, Canada
back:
• Ireland: Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), Method of President's election, Nomination of 12 members to Rajya Sabha.
• Australia: Concurrent List, Joint sitting of Parliament (Art 108), Freedom of trade & commerce.
• Weimar Germany: Suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency.
• USSR (Russia): Fundamental Duties (Art 51A), Ideals of Justice (Social, Economic, Political) in Preamble.
• South Africa: Constitutional Amendment procedure (Art 368), Election of Rajya Sabha members.
• Canada: Federation with strong Centre, Residuary powers to Centre (Art 248), Advisory jurisdiction of SC (Art 143).

front: Schedules 1 to 4: Territories, Salaries, Oaths, Rajya Sabha
back:
• 1st Schedule: Names of 28 States and 8 Union Territories and their territorial extent.
• 2nd Schedule: Provisions relating to Emoluments, allowances, and privileges of President, Governors, Speaker, Judges, CAG.
• 3rd Schedule: Forms of Oaths and Affirmations (Note: President's oath is in Art 60, not 3rd Schedule!).
• 4th Schedule: Allocation of seats in Rajya Sabha (Council of States) to States and UTs based on population (Highest: UP with 31 seats).

front: Schedules 5 & 6: Scheduled Areas & Special Tribal Areas
back:
• 5th Schedule: Administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes across states (Tribes Advisory Council).
• 6th Schedule: Special provisions for administration of tribal areas in 4 North-Eastern states: 'AMTM' (Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram) via Autonomous District Councils.

front: Schedule 7: The Three Federal Legislative Lists
back:
• 7th Schedule divides legislative powers between Centre and States into 3 Lists:
  1. Union List: Originally 97 subjects ➔ Currently 100 (Defence, Foreign affairs, Railways, Banking, Atomic Energy).
  2. State List: Originally 66 subjects ➔ Currently 61 (Police, Public health, Agriculture, Local government, Prisons).
  3. Concurrent List: Originally 47 subjects ➔ Currently 52 (Education, Forests, Marriage, Criminal law, Trade unions).
• Residuary powers belong to Parliament (Art 248).

front: Schedule 8: Official Languages of India & Amendments
back:
• Originally 14 languages ➔ Currently 22 Languages.
• Chronology of added languages:
  - 21st Amend (1967): Added Sindhi (15th).
  - 71st Amend (1992): Added Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali ('KMN') (16, 17, 18th).
  - 92nd Amend (2003): Added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali ('BDMS') (19, 20, 21, 22nd).
• Note: English and Rajasthani are NOT in the 8th Schedule!

front: Schedules 9, 10, 11, 12: Added by Amendments
back:
• 9th Schedule: Land reforms and abolition of Zamindari (Added by 1st Amendment 1951; protected from judicial review subject to Coelho case 2007).
• 10th Schedule: Anti-Defection Law (Added by 52nd Amendment 1985; decision by Speaker/Chairman).
• 11th Schedule: Panchayati Raj (Added by 73rd Amendment 1992; specifies 29 functional matters).
• 12th Schedule: Municipalities (Added by 74th Amendment 1992; specifies 18 functional matters).

front: Article 1: Name and Territory of the Union
back:
• Text: 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.'
• Key distinction: 'Union of States' rather than 'Federation of States' because the Indian federation is not the result of an agreement among states, and states have NO right to secede.
• Territory of India comprises: States, Union Territories, and acquired territories.

front: Article 2 vs Article 3: Admission vs Reorganization of States
back:
• Article 2: Admission or establishment of NEW states that are NOT part of India (e.g., Sikkim admitted in 1975).
• Article 3: Formation of new states, alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of EXISTING states within India (e.g., Telangana created in 2014, bifurcation of J&K in 2019).
• Procedure: Bill introduced only on recommendation of the President; passed by simple majority in Parliament.

front: Articles 5 to 11: Citizenship Provisions & Loss of Citizenship
back:
• Article 5: Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.
• Article 9: Person voluntarily acquiring foreign citizenship automatically loses Indian citizenship (No dual citizenship!).
• Article 11: Parliament has full power to regulate the right of citizenship by law (Citizenship Act 1955).
• 5 Ways to acquire citizenship: Birth, Descent, Registration, Naturalisation, Incorporation of territory.
• 3 Ways to lose citizenship: Renunciation, Termination, Deprivation.

front: Article 12 & Article 13: Definition of State & Judicial Review
back:
• Article 12: Defines 'State' for Part III (includes Govt & Parliament of India, Govt & Legislature of States, all local or other authorities like municipalities, panchayats, LIC, ONGC).
• Article 13: Declares all laws inconsistent with or in derogation of Fundamental Rights as NULL AND VOID.
• Foundation stone of Judicial Review in India.

front: Article 14: Equality before Law & Equal Protection of Laws
back:
• Equality before Law: British origin (Negative concept - absence of any special privilege; no man is above law).
• Equal Protection of the Laws: American origin (Positive concept - equality of treatment under equal circumstances).
• Applies to both citizens and foreigners, and legal entities (corporations, companies).

front: Article 15: Prohibition of Discrimination on 5 Grounds Only
back:
• Text: State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds ONLY of: Religion, Race, Caste, Sex, Place of birth (or any of them).
• Access to shops, public restaurants, wells, bathing ghats.
• Exceptions: Special provisions for women & children, SC/ST/OBC (Art 15(4)), and EWS (Art 15(6) via 103rd Amendment).

front: Article 16: Equality of Opportunity in Public Employment
back:
• Equal opportunity for all citizens in employment or appointment to any office under the State.
• No discrimination on 7 grounds: Religion, Race, Caste, Sex, Descent, Place of birth, Residence.
• Article 16(4): Reservation in posts for backward classes not adequately represented (Mandal Commission).
• Article 16(6): 10% EWS reservation in public jobs (103rd Amendment 2019).

front: Article 17 & Article 18: Untouchability & Abolition of Titles
back:
• Article 17: Abolition of 'Untouchability' (अस्पृश्यता का अंत) and prohibition of its practice in any form. Enforced via Protection of Civil Rights Act 1955. Absolute right!
• Article 18: Abolition of Titles (उपाधियों का अंत). State cannot confer titles except military and academic distinctions.
• Bharat Ratna, Padma awards are decorations, NOT titles under Art 18 (Balaji Raghavan case 1996).

front: Article 19: Protection of 6 Basic Freedoms
back:
• 6 Democratic Freedoms guaranteed to CITIZENS only:
  19(1)(a): Freedom of Speech and Expression (includes freedom of press & RTI)
  19(1)(b): Freedom to assemble peacefully and without arms
  19(1)(c): Freedom to form associations or unions or cooperative societies
  19(1)(d): Freedom to move freely throughout the territory of India
  19(1)(e): Freedom to reside and settle in any part of India
  19(1)(g): Freedom to practice any profession, trade, or business
• Note: 19(1)(f) (Right to Property) was deleted by 44th Amendment 1978.

front: Article 20: Protection in Respect of Conviction for Offences
back:
• 3 Cardinal Protections (Cannot be suspended even during Emergency!):
  1. No Ex-Post Facto Law: No person shall be convicted of any offence except under a law in force at the time of the act.
  2. No Double Jeopardy: No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once.
  3. No Self-Incrimination: No person accused of an offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself.

front: Article 21: Protection of Life and Personal Liberty & Landmark Cases
back:
• Text: 'No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.'
• A.K. Gopalan case (1950) ➔ Narrow interpretation.
• Maneka Gandhi case (1978) ➔ Expansive 'Due Process of Law' (Procedure must be just, fair, and reasonable).
• Expanded rights under Art 21: Right to privacy (Puttaswamy case 2017), Right to clean environment, Right to livelihood, Right to free legal aid, Right to speedy trial.
• Cannot be suspended during Emergency!

front: Article 21A: Right to Free and Compulsory Education
back:
• Added by: 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 2002.
• Text: State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of age 6 to 14 years.
• Enforcing Act: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act 2009 (came into effect on 1 April 2010).

front: Article 22: Protection Against Arrest and Preventive Detention
back:
• Rights of arrested person: Right to be informed of grounds of arrest, right to consult & be defended by a legal practitioner, right to be produced before Magistrate within 24 hours (excluding travel time).
• Preventive Detention: Detention without trial to prevent a person from committing a crime; maximum detention without advisory board approval is 3 months.

front: Article 23 & Article 24: Right against Exploitation
back:
• Article 23: Prohibition of traffic in human beings, 'begar' (forced labour), and other similar forms of forced labour.
• Article 24: Prohibition of employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories, mines, or hazardous occupations (Child Labour Prohibition Act 1986).

front: Articles 25 to 28: Right to Freedom of Religion
back:
• Article 25: Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion.
• Article 26: Freedom to manage religious affairs.
• Article 27: Freedom from payment of taxes for promotion of any particular religion (No religious taxation).
• Article 28: Freedom from attendance at religious instruction or worship in wholly state-funded educational institutions.

front: Article 29 & Article 30: Cultural and Educational Rights
back:
• Article 29: Protection of language, script, or culture of minorities (and any section of citizens).
• Article 30: Right of minorities (religious or linguistic) to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice ('Charter of Education Rights for Minorities').

front: Article 32: Right to Constitutional Remedies & Ambedkar's Quote
back:
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32: 'The very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it'.
• Direct approach to the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
• SC has power to issue Directions, Orders, or 5 Prerogative Writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo-Warranto.
• Fundamental Right itself!

front: DPSP Fundamentals & Article 37 (Non-Justiciability)
back:
• Borrowed from: Ireland (Irish Constitution 1937, who borrowed from Spain).
• Aim: To establish 'Socio-Economic Democracy' and a 'Welfare State' (कल्याणकारी राज्य).
• Article 37: DPSPs are NON-JUSTICIABLE (cannot be enforced by any court), but are 'fundamental in the governance of the country' and it shall be the duty of the State to apply them.

front: High-Yield DPSP Articles Checklist (39A, 40, 44, 48A, 50, 51)
back:
• Art 39A: Equal justice and free legal aid to the poor (NALSA Act 1987; added by 42nd Amend).
• Art 40: Organization of Village Panchayats as units of self-government (Gandhian).
• Art 44: Uniform Civil Code (UCC) for all citizens (Goa was 1st, Uttarakhand 1st post-independence).
• Art 48A: Protection and improvement of environment, forests, wildlife (added by 42nd Amend).
• Art 50: Separation of Judiciary from Executive in public services.
• Art 51: Promotion of international peace and security.

front: DPSP: Articles 41, 42, 43, 45, 47 (Socio-Economic Welfare)
back:
• Art 41: Right to work, education, and public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness.
• Art 42: Just and humane conditions of work & Maternity Relief.
• Art 43: Living wage, decent standard of life for workers.
• Art 43A: Participation of workers in management of industries (42nd Amend).
• Art 45: Early childhood care & education for children under 6 years (amended by 86th Amend).
• Art 47: Raise level of nutrition & standard of living; prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs harmful to health.

front: Article 51A: Fundamental Duties (Origins & Committee)
back:
• Borrowed from: USSR Constitution.
• Recommended by: Swaran Singh Committee (1976).
• Added by: 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1976 as Part IV-A (Article 51A).
• Originally 10 duties in 1976 ➔ 11th Duty added by 86th Amendment Act 2002.
• 11th Duty: Duty of parent/guardian to provide education opportunities to child aged 6 to 14 years.
• Like DPSPs, Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable.

front: President of India: Articles 52, 53, 54, 55 (Election)
back:
• Art 52: There shall be a President of India (Head of State, First Citizen).
• Art 53: Executive power of Union vested in President (Supreme Commander of Armed Forces).
• Art 54: Electoral College for President:
  - Elected members of Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha (Elected MPs)
  - Elected members of Legislative Assemblies of States (Elected MLAs)
  - Elected MLAs of Delhi & Puducherry (70th Amend 1992)
  - (Nominated MPs/MLAs and MLCs do NOT vote!).
• Art 55: Manner of election: Proportional representation by single transferable vote, secret ballot.

front: President: Qualifications (Art 58), Oath (Art 60), Impeachment (Art 61)
back:
• Art 58 Qualifications: Citizen of India, minimum 35 years old, qualified for election as Lok Sabha member, hold no office of profit.
• Art 60 Oath: Administered by Chief Justice of India (CJI) or seniormost SC judge.
• Art 61 Impeachment: Only ground is 'Violation of the Constitution'.
  - Initiated in either House (LS or RS) by 1/4th members signing 14-day notice.
  - Passed by Special Majority (2/3rd of TOTAL membership of that House).
  - Investigated by second House; if passed by 2/3rd total membership, President stands removed.
  - (No Indian President has ever been impeached).

front: Article 72: Pardoning Power of the President (5 Types)
back:
President has power to grant pardon for offences against Union law, Court Martial sentences, and Death sentences:
1. Pardon (क्षमा): Completely absolves sentence, conviction, and disqualifications.
2. Commutation (लघुकरण): Substituting one form of punishment with a lighter form (e.g. death ➔ life imprisonment).
3. Remission (परिहार): Reducing period of sentence without changing its character (e.g. 2 years rigorous ➔ 1 year rigorous).
4. Respite (विराम): Awarding lesser sentence on special grounds (pregnancy, disability).
5. Reprieve (प्रविलंबन): Temporary stay on execution of sentence (especially death penalty).

front: Article 123: President's Ordinance Making Power
back:
• Promulgated when: Parliament is not in session (either one or both Houses) and immediate action is required.
• Ordinance has same force and effect as an Act of Parliament.
• Maximum Life of Ordinance: 6 MONTHS + 6 WEEKS (must be approved within 6 weeks of Parliament's reassembly).
• Governor has parallel power under Article 213 for States.

front: Vice-President of India: Articles 63, 64, 66
back:
• Art 63: There shall be a Vice-President of India (2nd highest constitutional office).
• Art 64: VP is Ex-Officio Chairman of Council of States (Rajya Sabha).
• Art 66 Electoral College: All members of Parliament (both Elected + Nominated MPs of LS & RS; MLAs do NOT participate!).
• Qualifications: Citizen of India, min 35 years old, qualified for Rajya Sabha election.
• Acts as President in case of vacancy for a maximum of 6 months.

front: Articles 74, 75, 76: Council of Ministers, PM, and Attorney General
back:
• Art 74: Council of Ministers with PM at head to aid and advise President (advice is binding after 44th Amend).
• Art 75: PM appointed by President; other ministers appointed on advice of PM.
  - Ministers hold office during pleasure of President (individual responsibility).
  - Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the LOK SABHA (Art 75(3)).
  - 91st Amend 2003: Size of Council of Ministers shall not exceed 15% of total Lok Sabha strength.
• Art 76: Attorney-General for India (Highest Law Officer; right of audience in all courts; can participate in Parliament without right to vote).

front: Parliament Composition: Articles 79, 80, 81
back:
• Art 79: Parliament consists of: President + Council of States (Rajya Sabha) + House of the People (Lok Sabha).
• Art 80 Rajya Sabha: Max 250 members (238 elected from States/UTs + 12 nominated by President from Literature, Science, Art, Social Service). Permanent House; 1/3rd retire every 2 years; 6-year tenure.
• Art 81 Lok Sabha: Max 550 members (530 from States + 20 from UTs). 2 Anglo-Indian seats abolished by 104th Amendment 2020. Normal term: 5 years.

front: Articles 84 & 85: Membership Qualifications & Parliamentary Sessions
back:
• Art 84 Minimum Age: Lok Sabha member = 25 years | Rajya Sabha member = 30 years.
• Art 85 Sessions: Summoned by President; maximum gap between two sessions cannot exceed 6 MONTHS (minimum 2 sessions per year, usually 3: Budget, Monsoon, Winter).
• Terms: Prorogation terminates a session; Dissolution ends life of Lok Sabha (Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved).

front: Article 100: Quorum & Casting Vote of Speaker
back:
• Quorum (गणपूर्ति): Minimum number of members required to transact business in either House = 1/10th of total membership (LS: 55 members, RS: 25 members).
• Casting Vote: Speaker / Chairman does not vote in first instance, but exercises a casting vote in case of equality of votes (tie).

front: Article 108: Joint Sitting of Both Houses
back:
• Summoned by: The President in case of deadlock on an Ordinary Bill or Financial Bill.
• Presided over by: Speaker of Lok Sabha (in Speaker's absence, Deputy Speaker; if absent, Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha).
• Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Vice President) NEVER presides over a joint sitting!
• Bill passed by: Simple majority of total members present and voting.
• Joint sitting NOT applicable to: Money Bills (Art 110) & Constitutional Amendment Bills (Art 368).

front: Articles 109 & 110: Money Bill Special Procedure & Definition
back:
• Art 110 Definition: Relates only to imposition/abolition of tax, borrowing by government, custody/withdrawal from Consolidated Fund.
• Speaker of Lok Sabha has FINAL AUTHORITY to certify whether a bill is a Money Bill.
• Introduced ONLY in Lok Sabha, ONLY with prior recommendation of President.
• Rajya Sabha cannot amend or reject; can only suggest recommendations and delay for maximum 14 DAYS.

front: Article 112: Annual Financial Statement (Budget)
back:
• Word 'Budget' is NOWHERE mentioned in the Constitution of India; referred to as 'Annual Financial Statement'.
• Laid before Parliament by President showing estimated receipts and expenditures.
• Expenditure charged on Consolidated Fund of India is non-votable (salaries of President, SC judges, CAG).

front: Articles 124 to 143: Supreme Court Key Constitutional Provisions
back:
• Art 124: Establishment of Supreme Court (Currently 1 CJI + 33 Judges = 34; Retirement age: 65 years).
• Art 129: Supreme Court is a 'Court of Record' (power to punish for contempt of itself).
• Art 131: Original Jurisdiction (Federal disputes: Centre vs State, State vs State).
• Art 136: Special Leave to Appeal (SLP).
• Art 137: Power of Review of its own judgments.
• Art 141: Law declared by Supreme Court is binding on all courts within India.
• Art 143: Advisory Jurisdiction (President can seek SC's opinion; opinion is advisory, not binding).

front: Article 148: Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)
back:
• Appointed by: President of India (Warrant under hand and seal).
• Tenure: 6 years or up to 65 years of age (whichever is earlier).
• Known as: 'Guardian of the Public Purse' and friend, philosopher, and guide of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC).
• Removed: On same grounds and manner as a Supreme Court judge.
• Reports submitted to: President, who causes them to be laid before Parliament (examined by PAC).

front: Governor of a State: Articles 153 to 161
back:
• Art 153: There shall be a Governor for each State (7th Amend 1956 allows same person as Governor of two or more States).
• Art 155: Appointed by President.
• Art 156: Holds office during 'pleasure of the President' (no security of tenure; normal term 5 years).
• Art 157: Qualifications: Citizen of India, min 35 years old.
• Art 161: Pardoning power: Governor CANNOT pardon a death sentence (only President can under Art 72), and cannot pardon court-martial sentences.

front: Articles 168 & 169: State Legislature & Legislative Councils (Vidhan Parishad)
back:
• Art 169: Parliament can create or abolish Legislative Council in a State if State Assembly passes resolution by Special Majority (2/3rd present & voting).
• Only 6 States currently have Bicameral Legislature (Vidhan Parishad):
  1. Uttar Pradesh
  2. Bihar
  3. Maharashtra
  4. Karnataka
  5. Andhra Pradesh
  6. Telangana
  (Mnemonic: 'KUMBA-T')

front: High Courts: Articles 214 to 226
back:
• Art 214: High Court for each State (Parliament can establish common HC for two or more states - e.g. Punjab & Haryana HC, Guwahati HC).
• Current High Courts in India: 25 High Courts (25th is Andhra Pradesh HC at Amaravati).
• Retirement age of High Court judge: 62 years (SC judge is 65).
• Art 215: High Court to be a Court of Record.
• Art 226: Writ jurisdiction of High Courts (wider than Art 32 as it covers Fundamental Rights + other legal rights).

front: 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act 1992: Panchayati Raj
back:
• Added Part IX ('The Panchayats', Articles 243 to 243O) & 11th Schedule (29 matters).
• Historical Roots: Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957 - recommended 3-tier system).
  - First State to adopt: Rajasthan (Nagaur district, 2 Oct 1959 by Nehru), followed by Andhra Pradesh.
• Structure: 3-Tier (Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti / Block, Zilla Parishad).
• Key Provisions:
  - Art 243D: Reservation of min 1/3rd seats for women; SC/ST based on population.
  - Art 243I: State Finance Commission appointed every 5 years by Governor.
  - Art 243K: State Election Commission conducts local body elections.
  - Minimum age to contest: 21 years.

front: 74th Constitutional Amendment Act 1992: Municipalities
back:
• Added Part IX-A ('The Municipalities', Articles 243P to 243ZG) & 12th Schedule (18 functional matters).
• 3 Types of urban bodies: Nagar Panchayat (transitional area), Municipal Council (smaller urban area), Municipal Corporation (larger urban area).
• First Municipal Corporation in India: Madras (1687-88).
• Reservation of min 1/3rd seats for women (Art 243T).

front: Articles 248, 249, 262, 263: Centre-State Relations Highlights
back:
• Art 248: Residuary legislative powers vested in Parliament.
• Art 249: Power of Parliament to legislate on State List subject in national interest (if Rajya Sabha passes resolution with 2/3rd majority).
• Art 262: Adjudication of Inter-State River Water Disputes (Parliament can bar jurisdiction of courts; Cauvery, Krishna tribunals).
• Art 263: Inter-State Council (Constitutional body appointed by President; chaired by Prime Minister; Sarkaria Commission recommendation).

front: Articles 266, 267, 279A, 280, 300A: Financial Provisions
back:
• Art 266: Consolidated Fund of India (All revenues, loans; withdrawal requires Parliamentary approval via Appropriation Bill) & Public Account.
• Art 267: Contingency Fund of India (₹500 Cr default, enhanced to ₹30,000 Cr; held by Finance Secretary on behalf of President for unforeseen emergencies).
• Art 279A: GST Council (Added by 101st Amend 2016; chaired by Union Finance Minister).
• Art 280: Finance Commission (Appointed every 5 years by President; recommends tax devolution between Centre and States).
• Art 300A: Right to Property (Transferred from FR Art 31 by 44th Amend 1978; now a Legal / Constitutional Right).

front: Articles 312, 315, 323A: All India Services, UPSC & Tribunals
back:
• Art 312: All India Services (IAS, IPS, Indian Forest Service created in 1966). Can be created ONLY IF Rajya Sabha passes a resolution with 2/3rd majority.
• Art 315: Public Service Commission for Union (UPSC) and States (SPSC). Members appointed by President/Governor; tenure 6 years or 65 yrs (UPSC) / 62 yrs (SPSC).
• Art 323A: Administrative Tribunals (CAT - Central Administrative Tribunal created under 42nd Amend 1976).

front: Articles 324 to 326: Election Commission & Adult Suffrage
back:
• Art 324: Election Commission of India (ECI). Superintendence, direction, and control of elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President, and VP (Local body elections handled by State Election Commission!).
  - Composition: 1 Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) + 2 Election Commissioners.
  - CEC removed on same grounds as Supreme Court judge.
• Art 326: Universal Adult Suffrage. Right to vote given to every citizen aged 18+.
  - 61st Amendment Act 1988/89 reduced voting age from 21 to 18 years.

front: Articles 338, 338A, 338B: Constitutional National Commissions
back:
• Art 338: National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC).
• Art 338A: National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) (Bifurcated by 89th Amendment Act 2003).
• Art 338B: National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) (Conferred constitutional status by 102nd Amendment Act 2018).
• All submit annual reports to the President of India.

front: Articles 343 to 351: Official Language Provisions
back:
• Art 343: Official language of Union is Hindi in Devanagari script; numerals in international form of Indian numerals.
• Art 348: Language to be used in Supreme Court and High Courts is ENGLISH (until Parliament provides otherwise).
• Art 350A: Facilities for instruction in mother-tongue at primary stage.
• Art 350B: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (Appointed by President; created under 7th Amend 1956).
• Art 351: Directive for development and promotion of Hindi language.

front: Article 352: National Emergency (Proclamation, Grounds & Majority)
back:
• 3 Grounds: War, External Aggression, or Armed Rebellion (44th Amend 1978 substituted 'Armed Rebellion' for 'Internal Disturbance').
• Proclaimed by President ONLY on written advice of the Union Cabinet.
• Must be approved by both Houses within 1 MONTH by Special Majority (2/3rd present & voting + absolute majority).
• Extended by 6 months at a time (unlimited duration).
• Declared 3 times in India: 1962 (Chinese aggression), 1971 (Indo-Pak war), 1975 (Internal disturbance).

front: Articles 358 & 359: Effect of Emergency on Fundamental Rights
back:
• Art 358: Automatically suspends the 6 freedoms of Article 19 ONLY in case of National Emergency on grounds of WAR or EXTERNAL AGGRESSION (not armed rebellion).
• Art 359: Authorizes President to suspend right to move court for enforcement of other FRs, EXCEPT ARTICLES 20 AND 21 (Protected under 44th Amend 1978).
• Articles 20 & 21 can NEVER be suspended!

front: Articles 356 & 360: President's Rule & Financial Emergency
back:
• Art 356 President's Rule (State Emergency): Failure of constitutional machinery in State (report of Governor or otherwise under Art 365). Must be approved within 2 MONTHS by Simple Majority. Maximum period: 3 YEARS.
• Art 360 Financial Emergency: Threat to financial stability or credit of India. Approved within 2 months by Simple Majority. Salaries of judges and civil servants can be reduced. NEVER declared in India so far!

front: Article 368: 3 Methods of Constitutional Amendment
back:
• Borrowed from: South Africa.
• 3 Types of Amendments:
  1. By Simple Majority (Outside Art 368): Creation of new states, citizenship, official languages.
  2. By Special Majority (Under Art 368): Majority of total membership + 2/3rd present and voting (FRs, DPSPs).
  3. By Special Majority + Ratification by half of State Legislatures (Federal provisions): Election of President, SC/HC powers, distribution of legislative powers (7th Schedule), representation of states in Parliament, Art 368 itself.
• Joint sitting NOT permitted for Amendment Bills; President MUST give assent (24th Amend 1971).

front: 1st, 7th, 24th, 42nd, 44th Constitutional Amendments
back:
• 1st (1951): Added 9th Schedule to protect land reform laws from judicial review; placed reasonable restrictions on free speech.
• 7th (1956): Implemented State Reorganization Act (Fazal Ali Commission); 14 states & 6 UTs formed; common High Courts and Governor for multiple states.
• 24th (1971): Affirmed Parliament's power to amend any part of the Constitution including FRs; President's assent made obligatory.
• 42nd (1976): 'Mini Constitution'. Added Socialist, Secular, Integrity to Preamble; Part IV-A (Duties); Art 39A, 43A, 48A.
• 44th (1978): Restored democracy after Emergency; deleted Right to Property from FR; Art 20 & 21 immune during emergency; substituted 'Armed Rebellion'.

front: 52nd, 61st, 69th, 73rd, 74th Amendments
back:
• 52nd (1985): Anti-Defection Law (added 10th Schedule).
• 61st (1988/89): Reduced voting age from 21 years to 18 years for Lok Sabha and Assembly elections.
• 69th (1991): Designated Union Territory of Delhi as 'National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi' with 70-member Assembly.
• 73rd (1992): Constitutional status to Panchayati Raj (Part IX, 11th Schedule, 29 subjects).
• 74th (1992): Constitutional status to Urban Local Bodies (Part IX-A, 12th Schedule, 18 subjects).

front: 86th, 89th, 91st, 92nd, 97th Amendments
back:
• 86th (2002): Right to Education made Fundamental Right (Article 21A); amended Art 45; added 11th Fundamental Duty (Art 51A(k)).
• 89th (2003): Bifurcated National Commission for SC and ST into two bodies (NCSC Art 338 & NCST Art 338A).
• 91st (2003): Limited size of Council of Ministers to 15% of total Lok Sabha/Assembly strength (min 12 for States); strengthened anti-defection law.
• 92nd (2003): Added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali to 8th Schedule (18 ➔ 22 languages).
• 97th (2011): Constitutional status to Cooperative Societies (Part IX-B, Art 19(1)(c), Art 43B).

front: Recent Amendments: 99th, 100th, 101st, 102nd, 103rd, 104th, 105th, 106th
back:
• 99th (2014): NJAC (National Judicial Appointments Commission - Struck down as unconstitutional by Supreme Court in 2015).
• 100th (2015): Land Boundary Agreement with Bangladesh (exchange of enclaves).
• 101st (2016): Goods and Services Tax (GST) introduced (Art 279A).
• 102nd (2018): Constitutional status to National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC - Art 338B).
• 103rd (2019): 10% Reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in education and jobs (Art 15(6), 16(6)).
• 104th (2020): Extended SC/ST reservation in Lok Sabha and Assemblies for 10 years (until 2030); ceased reservation for Anglo-Indians.
• 105th (2021): Restored States' power to maintain their own State OBC lists.
• 106th (2023): 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam' - 33% reservation for women in Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
